newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The threat of a nation-wide strike has followed an indication by transport company FreightCorp that it will use management labour to break the picket line at Rio Tinto's Hunter Valley No 1 mine. The proposed strike is likely to shutdown ports, railways, mines and factories. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard is to deliver an agenda-setting policy statement next month that will focus on the potential of the Internet to create employment. The speech is expected to be based on the Information Policy Advisory Council report, which urges the Government to promote the growth of an online economy. Page 1.

Investor uncertainty about continued economic growth and doubt over the Reserve Bank's ability to deliver a further cut in official interest rates contributed to a bout of nervous selling on the sharemarket yesterday. The scepticism about the Reserve Bank's effectiveness has been sparked by the fall of local money market rates to below US levels for the first time since deregulation in the mid 1980s. Page 1.

A Reserve Bank study has found that Australians currently hold 40 per cent of their currency in A$100 bills, but consumers seem reluctant to spend them. The study, which appears in the July edition of the Reserve Bank's Bulletin, concludes that people view high-denomination notes as a way of storing wealth, or use them to trade in the underground economy. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Independent Senator Mal Colston and former WA Liberal Senator and powerbroker Noel Crichton-Browne have been charged with fraud and could face a maximum of ten years in jail. Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams announced yesterday that Colston and Crichton-Browne had been charged under the Crimes Act for abusing parliamentary entitlements. Page 1.

Two Australians, Greg Small and Yetty Bennett, were drowned after being trapped underwater when the temporary bridge they were crossing collapsed 7m into the river below. Small and Bennett were members of the Australian team attending the Israeli sporting event known as the "Jewish Olympics" and they were killed during the event's opening ceremony. Page 1.

The ACT Government is to face legal action from spectators of the botched demolition of the Royal Canberra Hospital. Melbourne law firm Slater and Gordon is preparing a compensation case on behalf of a family who witnessed the death of 12-year-old Katie Bender at the implosion. Page 4.

The Australian Taxation Office is pushing for reforms that would see taxpayers slugged with a new twin tax penalty worth a maximum of 22 per cent of their tax bills if they are late with their returns or payments. The reforms would ensure that ordinary taxpayers would face the same penalty rates as business for similar offences. Page 4.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Mal Colston is to be prosecuted for fraud over his abuse of parliamentary travel allowances. The action is expected to have serious consequences for the Federal Government as it will impede its ability to have legislation passed through the Senate. Page 1.

Sydney's Jewish community has gone into mourning over the death of two Australian athletes at the opening ceremony of the Maccabiah Games in Israel. Australia's Jewish ten-pin bowling champion, Gregory Small and ten-pin bowls team manager Yetty Bennett were killed when the bridge they were crossing collapsed. Page 1.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics yesterday released principal findings from the census conducted on 6 August, 1996. The census highlights trends such as an ageing population, a rise in the indigenous population, and the prevalence of debt among income earners. Page 1.

Former Liberal Minister Sir James Killen has recounted how the recently deceased Sir Garfield Barwick once told him the person he admired most was Captain James Cook. Killen was speaking at the private cremation service for Sir Garfield, held yesterday. page 1.
THE AGE

Independent Qld Senator Mal Colston is to be prosecuted on 24 counts of fraud against the Commonwealth relating to abuse of parliamentary travel entitlements. Along with WA Liberal Party powerbroker Noel Crichton-Browne, who faces two similar charges, he has been charged under section 29D of the Crimes Act. Page A1.

Australian athletes who marched to the opening ceremony of the Maccabiah Games in Israel have told of their fear as the bridge they were crossing collapsed underneath them and they fell into the polluted river below. Team manager Harry Procel described how the bridge fell apart slowly, giving people time to realise the horror of what was happening. Page A1.

The major findings of the 1996 census include a major population shift back to Melbourne, a sharp rise in the Aboriginal population, a significant fall in membership of Protestant denominations, and increasing numbers of people who claim they have no reliion. The Bureau of Statistics yesterday released the data, providing a snapshot of the nation. Page A1.

The Vic Government has appointed the first female judge to the Court of Appeal as part of its policy to increase the number of women in the judiciary. Dr Susan Kenny, QC, has worked as a constitutional, administrative and commercial lawyer, and will rank 10th on the State's highest court. Page A2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
